questions.question: Which engine dimension is the bore?
choices: The inside diameter of the cylinder.
The distance the piston travels from top to bottom.
The distance between adjacent cylinder centers.
The length of the connecting rod.
questions.answerText: The inside diameter of the cylinder.
questions.explanation:
Bore is the cylinder diameter; stroke is piston travel between top and bottom dead center.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is the stroke of a reciprocating engine cylinder?
choices: The piston travel from top dead center to bottom dead center.
The crankshaft speed in revolutions per minute.
The distance from the propeller flange to the firewall.
questions.answerText: The piston travel from top dead center to bottom dead center.
questions.explanation:
Stroke is the distance traveled by the piston between its two dead-center positions.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: For a four-cylinder engine, which expression gives total swept displacement?
choices: Four times the swept volume of one cylinder.
The clearance volume of one cylinder divided by four.
Fuel volume per minute times four.
questions.answerText: Four times the swept volume of one cylinder.
questions.explanation:
Total displacement is the sum of the swept volumes of all cylinders.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What does an engine compression ratio compare?
choices: Cylinder volume at bottom dead center with volume at top dead center.
questions.answerText: Cylinder volume at bottom dead center with volume at top dead center.
questions.explanation:
Compression ratio is the maximum cylinder volume divided by the minimum cylinder volume.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: Why must a reciprocating engine have a defined firing order?
choices: To distribute power impulses and loads through the crankshaft in the designed sequence.
To make every spark plug fire at the same instant.
To keep all pistons at top dead center together.
To set the propeller blade angle.
questions.answerText: To distribute power impulses and loads through the crankshaft in the designed sequence.
questions.explanation:
The firing order sequences combustion events to provide smooth operation and manage crankshaft loading.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What does brake horsepower represent?
choices: Power available at the engine output shaft after internal losses.
The theoretical power released by fuel before engine losses.
Electrical power used only by the starter.
The power absorbed by an accessory gearbox alone.
questions.answerText: Power available at the engine output shaft after internal losses.
questions.explanation:
Brake horsepower is measured at the output shaft and reflects power remaining after friction and pumping losses.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What does mean effective pressure provide when comparing reciprocating engines?
choices: A pressure measure representing the work-producing effect over a cycle.
The instantaneous pressure at the intake manifold only.
The oil pressure at the main bearing.
The pressure difference across the propeller.
questions.answerText: A pressure measure representing the work-producing effect over a cycle.
questions.explanation:
Mean effective pressure is a notional constant pressure that would produce the same work over the piston stroke.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the connecting rod in a reciprocating engine?
choices: Transmit force between the piston and crankshaft.
Meter fuel into the intake manifold.
Open and close the exhaust valve directly in every engine design.
Drive the magneto without a gear train.
questions.answerText: Transmit force between the piston and crankshaft.
questions.explanation:
The connecting rod transfers piston force to the crankshaft and transmits crankshaft motion back to the piston.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What motion does the crankshaft produce from the pistons in a reciprocating engine?
questions.answerText: Rotating motion.
questions.explanation:
The crankshaft converts reciprocating piston movement into rotation that can drive a propeller or gearbox.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: In a typical four-stroke engine, how many crankshaft revolutions occur during one cylinder operating cycle?
questions.answerText: Two.
questions.explanation:
The intake, compression, power, and exhaust strokes require two crankshaft revolutions.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the camshaft and valve train?
choices: Open and close the intake and exhaust valves at the correct times.
Change the propeller blade angle in flight.
Supply high voltage to the spark plugs.
questions.answerText: Open and close the intake and exhaust valves at the correct times.
questions.explanation:
Cam lobes and valve-train components time valve opening and closing relative to crankshaft position.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: Why are multiple cylinders commonly arranged in a radial engine?
choices: To provide several cylinders around a compact crankcase and a short, air-cooled engine package.
To eliminate the need for a crankshaft.
To ensure all cylinders fire at the same crank angle.
To make the engine operate without lubrication.
questions.answerText: To provide several cylinders around a compact crankcase and a short, air-cooled engine package.
questions.explanation:
Radial arrangement places cylinders around the crankcase and supports a relatively compact air-cooled design.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What does a gas-turbine engine spool refer to?
choices: A compressor-turbine assembly connected by a common shaft and rotating together.
A fuel nozzle and igniter pair.
A set of propeller blades controlled by a governor.
The exhaust duct downstream of the turbine.
questions.answerText: A compressor-turbine assembly connected by a common shaft and rotating together.
questions.explanation:
A spool is a mechanically connected compressor and turbine assembly; multi-spool engines have independently rotating assemblies.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: In a turbofan, what is bypass ratio?
choices: The mass airflow that bypasses the engine core divided by the mass airflow through the core.
The compressor pressure ratio divided by turbine temperature.
Fuel flow divided by total thrust.
Fan diameter divided by propeller diameter.
questions.answerText: The mass airflow that bypasses the engine core divided by the mass airflow through the core.
questions.explanation:
Bypass ratio compares bypass-stream airflow with core airflow.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: Which description best fits a turboshaft engine?
choices: It delivers most useful output as shaft power to drive a rotor or other load.
It produces thrust only through a high-speed exhaust jet.
It has no compressor or turbine.
It is a reciprocating engine with a free piston.
questions.answerText: It delivers most useful output as shaft power to drive a rotor or other load.
questions.explanation:
A turboshaft is optimized to deliver shaft power, commonly through a reduction gearbox.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.
